# Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro Review: An (Almost) True Hands-Off Helper

February 25, 2026

Review

Jin Soh

After spending some time with the [Xiaomi Air Purifier 6](https://nextrift.com/202542440/), it felt only natural to try another product from the brand’s ever-expanding smart home lineup. This time around, we have a robot vacuum, specifically the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro. With Xiaomi now several generations deep into robot vacuums, expectations are understandably higher, and this fifth-generation model is positioned as one of its more premium offerings.

The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro first launched in September last year and retails for **RM3399**. On paper, it checks most of the boxes you would expect from a high-end robot vacuum in 2025 going into 2026, including AI-powered obstacle recognition, high suction power and a self-cleaning dock. The question, as always, is how well any of this works in real-world use.

Design-wise, the Robot Vacuum 5 Pro looks largely like what you’d expect from a modern robot vacuum, with a familiar circular profile and a sizeable docking station. One standout feature, at least visually, is the dToF smart retractable radar, which lowers itself when the vacuum needs to clean under low furniture or in vertically limited spaces.

The vacuum itself houses a 5200mAh battery, which Xiaomi claims is good for up to 140 minutes of continuous cleaning, and it delivers a rather impressive 20,000Pa of suction power, all of this, of course, being on paper.

In daily use, the feature set is where the Robot Vacuum 5 Pro really starts to differentiate itself. Xiaomi’s AI obstacle avoidance system is capable of recognising over 200 types of objects, including smaller and more annoying household items like cables, socks, and even trailing plant leaves.

Combined with its AI dirt recognition, the vacuum can adjust its cleaning behaviour depending on what it detects on the floor, switching modes and intensity automatically instead of relying purely on user presets.

This intelligence is backed by a fairly sophisticated sensor setup. The vacuum uses a front-facing HD camera alongside an RGB camera, dual infrared cameras, and an infrared 3D dot projector to understand its surroundings in real time. In practice, this allows it to navigate confidently around furniture and obstacles while maintaining efficient cleaning paths.

The side brush and mop pads also automatically extend when needed, allowing the vacuum to clean closer to edges and corners than many older robot vacuums manage. For carpeted areas, ultrasonic detection lifts the mop pads to prevent dampening rugs, while the anti-tangle, self-cleaning dock takes care of dust disposal and basic maintenance without much user involvement.

Much of this experience is managed through the Xiaomi Home app, which remains one of the more mature smart home apps available. Mapping your home is straightforward, though not entirely foolproof. During my initial setup, I forgot to close the bathroom door, and the vacuum promptly rolled into the shower area, dropped down to the lower shower floor, and found itself unable to climb back out.

 

That, of course, required manual intervention, but once doors are closed or restricted zones are set within the app, cleaning becomes largely hands-off. You can customise room layouts, choose which areas to avoid, and decide whether the vacuum should vacuum, mop, or do both in a single run.

Suction strength can be adjusted between Silent, Standard, Strong, and Turbo modes. Standard strikes a good balance, remaining audible but not distracting, while Strong is still manageable for everyday use. Turbo is unmistakably loud but delivers when you really want maximum suction. Mopping water output has three adjustable levels and there’s also a live camera view if you want to monitor your home or keep an eye on pets.

 

The AI object detection is mostly accurate, though it did once mistake a trolley wheel for a shoe. Thankfully, these minor misclassifications don’t affect cleaning performance. There’s even a remote control mode if you want to manually drive the vacuum to a specific spot, or, if you’re feeling cheeky, around the house pet.

In terms of actual cleaning performance, the Robot Vacuum 5 Pro is generally thorough. It handles dust, hair, and everyday debris well, though you may occasionally spot a small dust ball that’s been rolled aside rather than sucked up. Obstacle avoidance is reliable, successfully navigating around furniture and loose cables most of the time.

That said, it did get stuck once when a sofa throw fell onto the floor without me realizing and tangled the brushes, requiring, once again, manual intervention. To Xiaomi’s credit, the vacuum immediately notified me that cleaning had paused and explained what needed to be done.

The self-cleaning dock uses disposable dust bags that are easy to find online, and better yet, they’re compatible with bags from older Xiaomi robot vacuum models. If you’ve been in the ecosystem for a while and still have a few spares lying around, they’ll work just fine here.

Inside the dock, you’ll find separate clean and dirty water tanks, both of which can be pulled out easily for refills or disposal. Xiaomi doesn’t mention the use of detergent in the water tanks but it’s probably best to stick to plain water as cleaning solutions could risk clogging the internal components over time.

Battery life is more than sufficient for most homes. In my roughly 900 square foot space, the vacuum completed a full cleaning run in about 50 minutes and still had more than 70 percent battery remaining. As expected for a robot vacuum with a self-cleaning dock, the footprint of both the vacuum and its base station is on the larger side. It’s not excessively bulky, but it does stand out visually and will require a dedicated corner with a nearby power outlet, which may be a consideration for smaller, more cramped homes.

At **RM3399**, the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro sits squarely in the premium segment. It’s priced similarly to the Roborock Qrevo C Pro while offering stronger suction, and it undercuts the RM3,800 Dreame L50 Ultra despite delivering a comparable set of features.

While the initial mapping process can come with a few hiccups, day-to-day operation is smooth once everything is set up. The size of the dock may also be a drawback for some, but if space allows, it’s a capable and largely hands-off cleaning solution.

If you’re already invested in the Xiaomi smart home ecosystem, the Robot Vacuum 5 Pro makes a lot of sense. Having everything managed through a single app adds a level of convenience, and overall, this fifth-generation model feels like a refinement of Xiaomi’s robot vacuum formula rather than a simple spec bump.

# Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro FAQ

**Product knowledge**

**Q1: What is liftable LiDAR on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The liftable laser radar is located directly above the robot vacuum. It is a laser radar component with a mechanical lifting structure. It achieves the core function of "balancing passability and high-precision perception" by dynamically adjusting the height.

When high-precision environmental modeling is required, the radar is raised to scan the surrounding space 360°. When entering low areas (such as under beds and sofas), the radar is lowered, allowing the device to lower its height to avoid collisions. This allows for low-lying passage, reduces the risk of getting stuck, and improves cleaning coverage.

The liftable LiDAR will lower when the main unit is idle, charging on the omni station, or cleaning low areas. When lowering to clean low areas, do not move the main unit to affect positioning.

**Q2: What is a collision buffer plate on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The collision buffer plate is located in the C-shaped movable board in front of the robot vacuum, which can pass through obstacles and protect the device and furniture by buffering.

The collision switch can be triggered to avoid obstacles. The collision buffer plate can be combined with other obstacle avoidance sensors to form a complete obstacle avoidance function.

**Q3: What is the structured light obstacle avoidance module on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The structured light obstacle avoidance module, also known as a line laser, is located at the front of the robot vacuum and is covered with a dark lens. It consists of a structured light obstacle avoidance sensor and a structured light projector.

The structured light obstacle avoidance module uses infrared laser emitters for intelligent obstacle avoidance. It is primarily used to sense obstacles in the surrounding environment in real time and plan paths. It supports the recognition of low obstacles (such as slippers and toys) to reduce collisions and jams.

**Q4: What is the AI triple-camera obstacle avoidance module on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The AI triple-camera obstacle avoidance module consists of an AI high-definition camera, an AI infrared camera, and an AI structured light projector. It's located directly in front of the robot vacuum. Compared to the structured light obstacle avoidance module, it offers the advantages of obstacle recognition, floor dirt detection, and video calling.

The AI triple-camera obstacle avoidance module uses infrared laser emitters for intelligent obstacle avoidance. It is primarily used to sense obstacles in the surrounding environment in real time and plan paths. It supports identifying low obstacles (such as slippers and toys) to reduce collisions or jams.

**Q5: What is an edge sensor on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The edge sensor is located on the front right side of the robot vacuum and is covered by a dark lens. It detects the distance to obstacles by sending and receiving infrared signals. It is primarily used to detect the edges of walls and furniture, allowing the robot vacuum to clean along these edges more efficiently, reducing collisions and enabling a "running close to the edge" feature.

**Q6: What is ultrasound on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The ultrasonic wave is located near the caster wheel at the bottom of the robot vacuum, and it determines the material of the ground by sending and receiving ultrasonic signals. It is mainly used to detect and distinguish different types of floor tiles, carpets, etc. By identifying the carpet, the functions of carpet avoidance, carpet lifting and carpet pressure cleaning can be realized.

**Q7: What is a cliff sensor on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: Cliff sensors are located at the bottom of the robot vacuum. There are 4 of them. They detect the height of the bottom by sending and receiving infrared signals to prevent the robot vacuum cleaner from falling from a high place and causing damage.

**Q8: What are the charging contacts on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The charging contacts are located at the rear of the robot vacuum and forms a pair with the charging electrode on the omni station. Charging is achieved through contact between the electrodes. The center area of the electrode is the infrared signal transceiver, ensuring accurate omni stationing when the robot vacuum returns to the omni station.

**Q9: What is the automatic water filling port on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The automatic water refill port is located on the rear of the robot vacuum, paired with the omni station water inlet. The initial mop cleaning will fill the main unit's small water tank with water. During mopping, the small tank keeps the mop moist, achieving constant-wet mopping. After the mop is complete, the small tank is completely drained.

**Q10: What is antiscalant on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: Antiscalants are used to inhibit the formation of scale from dissolved metal ions such as calcium and magnesium in water, preventing scale from accumulating inside the heating module and affecting the water heating function.

**Q11: What is a double scraper arm washboard on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The washboard has added a pair of scraping arms. When cleaning the mop pad, the double scraping arms are driven to rotate and clean the omni station, which is not easy to leave stains, reduces the odor of the omni station, and alleviates the trouble of frequent cleaning.

**Product usage**

**Q1: What are the buttons of the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro has an On/Off button, a recharge button, and a reset button.

**Q2: How to use the power button of the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: Press and hold the power button for 3s to turn on/off the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro.

Press it after turning on, to clean or pause.

**Q3: How to use the recharge button of the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

1. Press the recharge button of the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro during operation to enter pause state;

2. Press during pause to start recharging;

3. Press during recharging to stop recharging.

**Q4: How to turn on the child lock function of the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro?**

A: Press and hold the recharge button for 3 seconds to activate or deactivate the child lock.

**Note:**

When the child lock is turned on, the buttons on the robot vacuum will be invalid and can be controlled through the APP.

**Q5: What does the indicator of the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro mean?**

A: **The meanings of the indicator of the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro are as follows:**

White: Working/Work completed/Charging completed;

Flashing in white: Recharging/Repositioning/Firmware upgrading;

Breathing in white: Charging;

Breathing in orange: Charging (low battery);

Orange: Wi-Fi disconnected;

Flashing in orange: Abnormal status/Awaiting to connection/Wi-Fi connecting;

Purple: Microphone disabled;

Blue: Wi-Fi is connected;

Flashing in blue: Waiting for connection/Wi-Fi connecting;

Off: The device is not connected.

**Q10: What are the differences between the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro cleaning with and without a map?**

A: **The differences are as follows:**

1. Cleaning method when there is no map: When cleaning for the first time without a map, the robot vacuum will first extend the edge of a fixed area, and then use a bow-shaped cleaning method until all areas are covered;

2. Cleaning method after map: After starting, the robot vacuum will clean by room, starting with the side rooms. **Q11: Can the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro be charged continuously?**

The robot vacuum has overcharge protection and will automatically switch to a low current charge when fully charged.

**Q12: Does the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro have an overload protection function?**

A: All motors on the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro have overload protection function, including the main brush motor, side brush motor, main wheel motor, and mop motor. When foreign objects enter or serious blockage causes overload, the protection will automatically start to prevent motor damage. At the same time, the voice/APP will prompt the corresponding motor to be wound. Please follow the user manual instructions to promptly clean any tangled hair or foreign objects.

**Q13: What are the precautions when using the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro for the first time?**

A: **The precautions when using the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 5 Pro are as follows:**

1. Before use, press and hold the On/Off button on the robot vacuum for 3 seconds to turn on the device;

2. After turning on the device, align the charging contacts of the robot vacuum with the charging spring of the omni station;

3. When you hear the voice announcement that charging has started, the main unit is successfully connected to the omni station;

4. Please fully charge the main unit before starting to clean from the omni station. Before cleaning, please tidy up your home furniture and put away fragile items and debris on the floor in advance.
